newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen consolidating next week.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen consolidating next week.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to consolidate next week in thin pre-holiday trade, after it was boosted on Friday by gains on Wall Street and a firm bond market.
"We will have to work at keeping our gains," said one dealer. "But the basic trend should be generally positive."

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day dealings in the DAX index of leading shares, pared gains in late trade to stand up 14.73 points, or 0.52 percent at 2,839.56 points by 1544 GMT, as Wall Street tracked back from early highs and the dollar came off its highs of the day.
The DAX had earlier closed floor trade at 2,854.45 points, breaking out of the narrow trading range of recent days.
Dealers said the settlement of the DAX December future contract and the expiry of options on its constituent stocks, so-called triple witching, had helped boost the market.
Dealers said shares in Siemens, the most heavily traded during the day, had been subject to expiry volatility.

Some dealers said the day's rally meant the 2,900 point level was once again in sight for the DAX index for the year-end, but others were more cautious and said the index would probably end the year around current levels.

The German markets are closed on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday next week for Christmas. DAX gainers, boosted after the company said it had received clearance from the German Federal Cartel Office for its pending acquisition of U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp.

The stock was also encouraged by news out after Thursday's bourse close that the group plans to acquire the remaining 23 percent of consumer products group Hans Schwarzkopf it does not already own. Henkel preference shares ended bourse dealings up over four percent, or 3.30 marks at 76.90 marks.
